outcomes: Identify various industry subsectors—including biomanufacturing, synthetic biology, and cell therapy—and examine the educational transitions and professional certifications required to navigate the California biotechnology workforce.
Execute foundational laboratory procedures, such as genomic DNA extraction and protein purification, while adhering to strict OSHA-standard safety protocols and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

Appraise the function of quality management systems (such as GMP) and distinguish between upstream and downstream processing to understand how bioscience products move from development to the marketplace.

Develop strategies for effective leadership, communication, and workplace inclusion while assessing how lean startup principles and intellectual property rights address unmet needs within the biotech industry.
